name: Ishmael
description: Jeremiah's adversary living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and the people fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, killing a man who gave wise counsel.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Johanan the son of Kareah and the captains of the forces came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and warned him that Baalis the king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay him, but Gedaliah believed them not.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: Johanan spoke secretly to Gedaliah, offering to kill Ishmael himself so that Gedaliah would not be slain and the gathered remnant scattered.
Gedaliah forbade Johanan to do it, saying he spoke falsely of Ishmael, and refused to believe the plot.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: In the seventh month Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed and a prince of the king, came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they ate bread together at a banquet held in Ishmael's honor.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ishmael and his ten men rose up and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam with the sword and slew him, the governor the king of Babylon had made over the land.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ishmael also slew all the Jews with Gedaliah at Mizpah and the Chaldeans and men of war that were found there.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ishmael went out from Mizpah weeping as he met them, playing a part, and invited them in to Gedaliah; when they came into the midst of the city he and his men slew them and cast them into a pit.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ten of the eighty were spared when they told Ishmael they had hidden treasures of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the field.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: The pit Ishmael filled with the slain was the one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel during the war between them.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people at Mizpah, including the king's daughters, whom Nebuzaradan had committed to Gedaliah, and departed toward the Ammonites.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: When Johanan and the captains heard of all the evil Ishmael had done, not only killing Gedaliah but at least eighty other men, they took their men and went to fight him and found him by the great waters in Gibeon.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: All the people Ishmael had taken captive were glad to see Johanan, turned about, and returned to him, but Ishmael escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: Johanan took the whole remnant he had recovered from Ishmael, the mighty men of war, the women, the children, and the eunuchs, and departed to dwell near Bethlehem on the way toward Egypt.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

points: They set out to seek refuge in Egypt because they were afraid of the Chaldeans, since Ishmael had slain Gedaliah whom the king of Babylon had made governor; with Gedaliah dead they felt they had no reason to stay.

note.label: Jeremiah 41: Ishmael Murders Gedaliah and Johanan Recovers the Remnant

cases.name: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah
cases.charge: Smiting Gedaliah the governor with the sword at his own table, and all the Jews and Chaldeans with him at Mizpah; slaying seventy of the eighty men coming with offerings to the house of the Lord and casting them into the pit; carrying the residue captive toward the Ammonites
cases.preview: After Jerusalem fell, the king of Babylon made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor at Mizpah over the poor left in the land;
